incidents.victim: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party service provider's platform to gain direct access to the bank's own account and systems.
incidents.impact: Hackers used the bank's own account to transfer an estimated $133 million to other institutions and convert funds into cryptocurrency; some assets have since been frozen and customer accounts were not affected.

incidents.victim: Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 industrial device operators
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-58115, a missing-authentication flaw (CVSS 10.0) in the Node-RED admin interface of Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices, to deploy wget/curl-based Linux bot malware.
incidents.impact: Unpatched, internet-exposed industrial controllers were compromised and infected with bot malware despite a vendor patch available since August 2026.

incidents.victim: Amadeus IT Group (affecting Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Air, Asiana Airlines, Singapore Airlines, Malaysia Airlines, Qantas, All Nippon Airways)
incidents.vector: Attackers used login credentials assigned to a system account to access a vulnerability in a travel booking display environment operated by IT provider Amadeus.
incidents.impact: Booking-display data — including passenger names, flight details, confirmation numbers, and in some cases passport and frequent-flyer data — was exposed for well over 200,000 passengers across multiple airlines; no payment data or airline operational systems were affected.

incidents.victim: The Kyiv Independent
incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to the outlet's website content management system and its newsletter distribution service.
incidents.impact: Attackers published false messages and sent disinformation emails to subscribers, including fabricated nuclear-strike and assassination claims about President Zelensky; banking and donor payment information was not compromised.

incidents.victim: Global consumers and businesses (1.3M+ Android TV set-top boxes and IoT devices)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — IoT botnet operator (Videostrong Technology Co.)
incidents.vector: China-based device manufacturer Videostrong deliberately embedded the "XCPE" backdoor in Android TV boxes and other IoT devices, evading Android security review via obfuscation, then sold criminal affiliates access to deploy their own malware modules.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million devices — including telehealth equipment and digital signage — were enrolled in a backdoor network used for ad fraud, residential-proxy resale, screenshot capture, and keystroke injection; Google disrupted the infrastructure and banned Videostrong from the Android ecosystem.

incidents.victim: UK school estate (multiple affiliated schools)
incidents.vector: Attacker stole backup credentials, created rogue domain-admin accounts, established Active Directory trusts between schools, and used living-off-the-land tools with AI-assisted command generation to move laterally.
incidents.impact: Ransomware was deployed across multiple schools within a shared estate after data theft; researchers assessed an AI model likely handled repetitive command generation and troubleshooting alongside a human operator.

incidents.victim: Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) users running outdated versions
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a DSM vulnerability (Synology-SA-24:20) patched in December 2024 but still unpatched on many devices.
incidents.impact: Ransomware was deployed against Synology NAS devices still running outdated, vulnerable DSM software.

incidents.victim: European supermarkets and food suppliers (Carrefour, Ahold Delhaize, Colruyt Group, Coop, AIMS members, Langridge Organic, and others across 12+ countries)
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed internet-exposed refrigeration supervisory controllers (Copeland XWEB, Danfoss AK-SM 800A, Dixell) via known, unpatched authentication-bypass vulnerabilities and weak default credentials.
incidents.impact: Fridges and freezers at dozens of supermarkets and suppliers across a dozen European countries were switched to defrost mode, raising temperatures to roughly 50°C and spoiling stock; a prior wave caused losses estimated in the tens of millions of dollars.

incidents.victim: cPGuard customers (cPanel / shared hosting providers)
incidents.vector: Attacker used stolen credentials to access OPSSHIELD's cPGuard update servers and inject a malicious update.
incidents.impact: Malicious cPGuard versions 5.88.12–5.88.19 collected /etc/shadow, MySQL configuration files, root shell history, SSH keys, and known-hosts files from customer servers.

incidents.victim: Mercado Bitcoin
incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
incidents.impact: Approximately $49 million in crypto assets were stolen; the exchange froze about $11 million and pledged to refund affected users.

incidents.victim: Ukraine's national air raid alert application
incidents.vector: Hackers compromised the widely used air raid alert app's alert-messaging system.
incidents.impact: Fabricated warnings of nuclear and chemical strikes and street fighting were pushed to app users nationwide, directing some toward a Telegram channel tied to a previously unknown group calling itself Hitcore Corp.

incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: Multi-stage social engineering campaign: a malicious Homebrew install compromised one engineer, then a fake job-interview process with a malicious coding test compromised a second, whose access was used with an internal AI tool to escalate control over wallet engineering staff.
incidents.impact: Approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency across 11 tokens was stolen — the largest cryptocurrency theft on record; Binance recovered roughly 95% of the funds' value from its own reserves and froze $2.8 billion in stablecoins, leaving about $3.25 billion believed to be undergoing laundering.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS customers with internet-exposed management interfaces
incidents.vector: Attackers chained the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw against internet-facing PAN-OS management interfaces to gain root access.
incidents.impact: Roughly 0.02% of Palo Alto Networks' global installed base with internet-facing management interfaces was affected; Palo Alto Networks individually contacted and remediated each impacted customer.

incidents.victim: South Korean financial institutions and roughly 80 Japanese companies
incidents.vector: Threat actors used the Chinese open-source AI penetration-testing tool ARTEX — in one case combined with the DeepSeek LLM and a second commercial LLM — to automate reconnaissance and intrusion against multiple organizations.
incidents.impact: Dozens of South Korean financial institutions and about 80 Japanese companies were targeted, with 8 of the Japanese intrusions occurring in the 30 days before disclosure.

incidents.victim: Organizations in space/satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research
incidents.vector: Threat actor UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, to deploy a custom malware framework ("KeyDrift") inside SD-WAN control-plane processes.
incidents.impact: KeyDrift provided long-term persistent access and automated exfiltration of sensitive IPsec keying material and control-session metadata; the operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with a covert access network previously linked to Chinese state-sponsored activity.

incidents.victim: Philippine Overseas Employment Administration
incidents.vector: Attacker used privilege-escalation tools (GodPotato, SeImpersonate) and the Impacket library to access and exfiltrate SQL Server database backups via a Singapore-based staging server.
incidents.impact: Nearly 69GB of data was exfiltrated in 24 minutes, including overseas-employment case records, contracts, accreditation data, and financial/cashier records on migrant workers.

incidents.victim: Members of the German Parliament, including staff of Chancellor Merz
incidents.vector: Mercenary spyware was deployed against targets' devices; the campaign was discovered after Apple issued threat notifications to affected individuals.
incidents.impact: German officials' devices were targeted with commercial-grade spyware, prompting an investigation by Germany's federal cybersecurity agency (BSI).

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached government IT systems and began extracting data before being detected by government IT staff.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly one-third of Moldova's population was stolen; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: Sourcenext
incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the company's member information retrieval API.
incidents.impact: 22,519,960 customer records were compromised, including email addresses, passwords, names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and employment information.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime operators, and global shipping companies (via CyberLogitec, a South Korean maritime IT provider)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware / data extortion (n0n group)
incidents.vector: A supply-chain attack on maritime IT services provider CyberLogitec was used to pivot into the networks of its downstream customers.
incidents.impact: More than 40 port authorities, maritime, and shipping companies were listed on the group's dark web leak site after a payment deadline expired.

incidents.victim: IDCFrontier (Japanese cloud provider) and its downstream customers
incidents.vector: Ransomware was deployed against Japanese cloud provider IDCFrontier's infrastructure.
incidents.impact: 495 companies and local governments relying on IDCFrontier's cloud services were disrupted.
